5.content: and that of the Mother of

spiritual_reading:
The ordered turning of general knowledges in the outer mind, which has been shown to you, is a great and mighty arrangement. It is one of four universal arrangements, for the whole government of states in the created mind is distinguished into four comprehensive domains.

The first domain is the operative forces active in the higher degrees of the mind, and the ruling capability confined within those degrees, held as in restraint within the interiors that are above the outward turning.

The second domain is the lower degrees beneath, the mixed and compounded planes of life, and the obscurities where truth is absent and falsity reigns. This domain extends from the life in which the human being acts in the bodily and worldly state down toward the lowest plane.

The third domain is the ultimate boundaries and containing forms that encompass the distinct levels of one’s spiritual world. It is the elevated states and the full series of discrete degrees that contain what is within them, together with the ruling capability confined within those containments, and the subordinate forces that preside over them.

The fourth domain is the ordered complex of general knowledges in externals, set in meticulous arrangement as a patterned whole of the living principles of love and wisdom.

This external complex is held in exact order because of the great and cruel forces of perverted love and the gigantic falsities of persuasion that are fastened within it and dependent upon it. Therefore the first outbirths and chief beginnings of all dominant evils—those that had been active in the three domains—were gathered together, seized, restrained, and fixed into this external turning. Each was allotted its place according to the three domains. They were arranged in interwoven connection, and made to balance against others of like measure.

Yet this external turning is equal to them in strength, for it bears the restrained forces of enmity fixed within it. They were fastened into this ceaseless motion because of their cruelty, so that through restless change and unstable agitation they do not perceive the state in which they are set. For if they had been restrained in higher interiors, those interiors could not have borne their weight; and if they had been fixed in the lowest planes, those planes likewise could not have borne them. Instead they were suspended in the circling of outward knowledges, so that the power and illumination rising from lower uses could be received and communicated to the higher interiors above. Conversely, whatever influx descends from above—whether chilling denial or burning craving—this external complex also receives it and disperses it through the whole lower life, into every form of perception.

Behold, the ordering of this external turning is of this nature. For the forces interwoven within it are like this: as though the governing love of a person rules its whole domain by means of a mighty host of leading intentions, together with all the defensive falsities and persuasive appearances gathered to support it, and also the mass of knowledges and delights of possession that it claims as its own, and the pleasing allurements of cupidities drawn together to serve it, along with other acquisitions and the dispersed appetites that attend its train. Yet if one inquires into that governing love, it is equal in measure to all that serves it; and what serves it is, in turn, equal in effect to the whole domain it rules. From it proceed decision and assessment—both acquittal and condemnation—through the entire mind, by the quality of its understanding, its practiced capacity, and its prevailing force.

As it is with such a governing love, which is equal to the measure of its whole domain by its understanding, practiced capacity, and prevailing force, so it is with the restrained forces fixed in the outward complex when compared with the ruling capability, and with the forces present through the whole expanse of one’s created order. As that governing love stands to its attendants, so the whole of this outer arrangement gathers into dominant principles: into a complete process and into a full organization of truths in the natural degree. As all specific teachings and practices gather to the ruling love, so they gather again to the chief determinants of the universal state. Everything done in the whole mind, above and below—conflicts, confusions, captivities, deprivation of truth, disordered craving, and the possession of knowledges—rises and falls according to these determinants. They are the movers of the entire created order, the whole being gathered into them as has been told you; thus the understanding is opened.

fills.notes: The phrase must read “in a foremany …” i.e., in a very great plurality and patterned multiplicity. This matches the correspondential sense: the sphere is an ordered complex, not a single thing, and it is arranged in a ‘patterned whole’. The surviving final m- fits the common Coptic-English rendering “foremany”.

Completes the thought: the star-sphere is ‘ordered in a foremany orderings’, i.e., structured in numerous distinct arrangements. This suits the oldest substrate’s impersonal cosmological register (structural arrangement), and matches the spiritual sense of a meticulous patterned whole.

fills.fill: and that of the Mother of Life
fills.notes: Restores the standard dyad in the oldest cosmological layer: Father of Life paired with Mother of Life (not ‘Mother of the living’, which leans later and more devotional). The spiritual translation already treats them as living principles of love and wisdom; ‘Mother of Life’ is the more archaic, structural title.
“Its ordinance … with diligence” gives the required impersonal, structural statement: the wheel’s arrangement is kept in strict order. This aligns with the spiritual sense: ‘held in exact order’.
Yields: “Its ordinance … [is] very ordered with diligence,” directly matching the spiritual sense ‘held in exact order … with diligence’.

The list is a catalogue of a king’s gathered supports; after ‘together with’ the text needs a general totalizing determiner before ‘property’, matching the spiritual sense ‘along with other acquisitions’.

Balances the catalogue: “together with all the property besides …” i.e., further acquisitions beyond the already-mentioned mass of property. This preserves the impersonal, enumerative style of the substrate and matches the spiritual sense of ‘other acquisitions’.
Smooths the final item: “and those cattle also that have been distributed …” marking an additional, dispersed class of possessions (appetites/attendants in the spiritual sense).

assessment: Most restorations are structurally constrained by the chapter’s fourfold scheme and by the repeated emphasis on meticulous ordering. The dyad ‘Father of Life’ and ‘Mother of Life’ is strongly demanded by the oldest cosmological register, so that restoration is relatively tight. The three small lacunae in ¶8 sit inside an expansive simile-catalogue; correspondentially their function is clear (additional acquisitions and dispersed attendants), but the exact connective particles are less constrained, so those remain tentative.
